correctness.rationale: The three diagonal quadrics are a smooth genus-five complete intersection for five distinct branch values; this follows because at most one coordinate vanishes at any point and any four relevant gradient columns span rank three. The order-sixteen sign group yields five genus-one character quotients, and its 2-power isogeny has invertible degree in characteristic three. In Legendre form the Hasse coefficient is -(1+lambda), with exactly one supersingular fourth point after a fixed triple. Two different four-subsets share three points, so at most one elliptic factor is supersingular. Its a-number is one and p-rank zero; the other factors are ordinary, giving the listed rank, a-number and Newton polygons. The five Hasse components each omit one branch label, are mutually disjoint smooth four-punctured projective lines, and have simple Hasse zero. Counting those F_q-rational points proves the formulas for all n>=1. A standalone stdlib checker exhaustively verified q=3,9,27; these experiments are not substituted for the universal argument.

originality.rationale: Source arXiv:1609.04895 establishes the five-point Humbert model and fields of moduli over complex curves, not the characteristic-three Hasse divisor. Source arXiv:1905.12690, Theorems 2.1 and 4.1, gives the five elliptic factors and power-of-two isogeny, which is used as prior art, but supplies neither the unique characteristic-three harmonic completion nor the absence of intersections nor all-extension marked counts. The characteristic-three supersingularity calculation and combinatorial compatibility are additional inputs. Three actual mathematical-record queries located no equal or stronger result. The closest accessible historical abstract (Yamauchi 2008) treats split Jacobians over number fields; its full text was not read, leaving historical overlap risk. Absence of search hits is not a uniqueness certificate.

value.rationale: This is a complete p-rank/Newton and Hasse-locus classification on the natural two-dimensional marked moduli surface of genus-five Humbert curves in characteristic three. The pairwise disjointness of all five supersingular-quotient divisors contrasts with possible intersecting component loci in other characteristics and gives a genuine geometric compatibility obstruction. Each component has its own explicit rational parametrization, and the theorem derives exact counts over every finite extension without numerical fitting. It is neither an isolated parameter substitution nor a finite table only.
